articles.title: Volkanovski, Evloev's Next Best Fights After UFC 333 Results
articles.summary: Alexander "The Great" Volkanovski remained the UFC featherweight champion with a second-round technical knockout win over Movsar Evloev at UFC 333.
articles.body:
Alexander "The Great" Volkanovski remained the UFC featherweight champion with a second-round technical knockout win over Movsar Evloev at UFC 333.

Volkanovski, 38, continues to defy the conventional wisdom of aging in the 145-pound division. In a weight class that is usually dominated by younger talent, he just set the record for most UFC featherweight title wins with nine.

The champion's win streak since losing back-to-back title fights against Islam Makhachev and Ilia Topuria has added another impressive chapter to his legacy.

Now the division's focus turns to who is next. The division has a few interesting contender and there is, of course, the opportunity for superfights for a star like Volkanovski.

Aljamain Sterling vs. Kevin Vallejos winner

What is left for Volkanovski to prove? That's the driving question behind what is best for the champion.

He's already made his case as the most dominant featherweight of all time. Adding another title defense there will just pad a legacy that is already established.

The 38-year-old has already done what he can do in the division. What he hasn't done is make a successful move up to lightweight. He gave Islam Makhachev a tough five-round fight in his first attempt and was knocked out in the first round of the rematch.

A fight against Justin Gaethje would give Volk one last shot at being a two-division champion. He's already called for the fight publicly.

If Gaethje isn't interested and the champion has to stay at featherweight, then Jean Silva is the cleanest matchmaking. The Brazilian is 7-1 since siging with the UFC in 2024 and he doesn't have a fight booked.

If brass feels like he hasn't done enough then the winner of the scheduled Nov. 21 bout between Aljamain Sterling and Kevin Vallejos should be considered.

Kevin Vallejos vs. Aljamain Sterling loser

Movsar Evloev came up short in his first title bid, but this isn't the last we've seen of him. The 32-year-old earned his title shot with a 20-0 record that included wins over Lerone Murphy, Arnold Allen and Aljamain Sterling.

Of course, some of those names are still toward the top of the pecking order in the weight class. Rematches could be inevitable, but Jean Silva stands out as the top option that wouldn't be a rematch.

Silva has potential as the next title challenger. He's 7-1 since his UFC debut in 2024. If Volkanovski decides to pursue the lightweight title again then it would make sense for Silva to fight Evloev to sort out the division.

Evloev could also have his eye on the Nov. 21 bout between Kevin Vallejos and Sterling. He already has a win over Sterling, though, so Vallejos would be the more intriguing matchup.

Youssef Zalal would be a bit of a bounce-back fight. He's coming off a loss to Sterling, but he's another ranked option that doesn't have a fight scheduled right now.

Volkanovski breaks record after title win at UFC 333

articles.title: Alexander Volkanovski Delivers Brutal Finish to End Movsar Evloev’s 20-0 Streak at UFC 333
articles.summary: Alexander Volkanovski registered a record 9th title fight win in the featherweight division in the main event of UFC 333.
articles.body:
For Alexander Volkanovski , age is just a number. The Australian successfully defended his featherweight title against Movsar Evloev at UFC 333 , handing the previously undefeated Russian his first career loss with a brutal second-round TKO at 4:54 at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi.

As expected, Volkanovski's sharp striking and incredible takedown defense proved to be the difference. The 38-year-old looked quicker on the feet from the opening bell, attacking Evloev's legs with inside low kicks before mixing in stiff jabs and powerful overhand rights. Whenever the Russian managed to take the fight to the ground, Volk bounced back to his feet almost immediately.

Evloev had some success with his wrestling in the opening round, repeatedly attempting takedowns and briefly dragging the champion to the canvas. However, Volkanovski kept escaping and landing clean shots on the feet. Evloev also managed to connect with a solid left hook during an exchange near the cage, but the Australian continued to press forward and dictate the pace.

The fight took a dramatic turn in the second round. Evloev once again tried to use his wrestling to slow the champion down, grabbing a body lock and dragging him to the canvas. However, Volkanovski quickly reversed the position, landed some ground-and-pound, and returned to striking range.

The champion then began to find his rhythm, connecting with a powerful overhand right that appeared to hurt Evloev. A blistering combination followed, with a left hand wobbling the Russian before another heavy shot sent him crashing toward the canvas.

With Evloev badly hurt and covering up, Volkanovski unleashed a barrage of punches and hammerfists until referee Marc Goddard stepped in to stop the fight with just seconds remaining in the round. The Russian entered the matchup with a perfect 20-0 record, but the champion proved too much for him to overcome.

The victory was another major milestone in Volkanovski's legendary career. He recorded his ninth UFC featherweight title-fight victory, surpassing Jose Aldo's divisional record and strengthening his case as the greatest fighter in the division's history.

Since reclaiming the belt at UFC 314, the 38-year-old has now successfully defended it twice. His latest victory also extended his winning streak to three fights, following back-to-back title-fight wins over Diego Lopes.

Moreover, Volkanovski gave no indication that he was ready to walk away from the sport. Speaking to Daniel Cormier after the fight, the Australian praised Evloev but made it clear that he always backed himself to get the job done.

He said, "He's a great fighter. He was undefeated for a reason, but I just said I'm the right guy for that job. I knew the ref would have to stop it when he covered up like that."

The 145-pound kingpin also opened up about his future, suggesting that he could continue fighting as long as he feels good and avoids taking too much damage.

The Aussie added, "I'm choosing to do this. I said if I didn't take too much damage, we probably keep going, so maybe we keep going. I feel the love, and it's paid off now. The love around the world is incredible."

With several contenders waiting for their shot at featherweight gold, including Jean Silva, Aljamain Sterling, and Kevin Vallejos, Volkanovski has no shortage of potential challengers. However, a move back to lightweight could also be on the cards, with a third attempt at 155 pounds potentially setting up a blockbuster showdown against Justin Gaethje as a fitting send-off fight.

articles.title: Latest UFC odds: Justin Gaethje opens as betting favorite to smash Alex Volkanovski … but not by much
articles.summary: Reigning UFC featherweight champion Alex Volkanovski retained his 145-pound title by smashing and trashing Movsar Evloev atop the UFC 333 MMA event earlier t...
articles.body:
Reigning UFC featherweight champion Alex Volkanovski retained his 145-pound title by smashing and trashing Movsar Evloev atop the UFC 333 MMA event earlier today in Abu Dhabi, handing the Russian his first loss in 21 professional fights.

So what's next for the 38-year-old Aussie?

Volkanovski (29-4) already holds two face-sitting victories over No. 2-ranked Diego Lopes, and No. 3-ranked Lerone Murphy is coming off a loss to Evloev at UFC London back in March . Perhaps No. 5-ranked Jean Silva — a popular fan favorite — could land the next crack at the 145-pound crown.

Or the winner of Aljamain Sterling ( No. 4 ) vs. Kevin Vallejos ( No. 10 ).

If Volkanovski had his way, he'd be elevated to No. 1 contender at 155 pounds , leapfrogging Ilia Topuria and Arman Tsarukyan for the chance to unseat Justin Gaethje and claim the lightweight throne. While it sounds far-fetched, UFC CEO Dana White appears to be on board.

"This guy's accomplished so much, it's hard to say no to a guy like that," White said . "When a guy gets to his level, there aren't too many things we'd say 'no' to him about. If he's got things he wants to do before he hangs it up, I'm sure we'll be very supportive."

Volkanovski already tried his hand at lightweight and came up short both times .

That may be one of several reasons BetOnline.ag opened Volkanovski as the +157 underdog against -180 for Gaethje. "The Great" recently posed the "Highlight" fight as a potential retirement bout for both combatants , though Gaethje remains on the fence about his fighting future.

Based on his destruction of Ilia Topuria at UFC White House , it appears Gaethje still has plenty left in the tank.

articles.title: 'The FW GOAT': Alexander Volkanovski's unreal UFC 333 knockout has fighters talking all-time greatness
articles.summary: Alexander Volkanovski just keeps finding ways to add to his legend.
articles.body:
Alexander Volkanovski just keeps finding ways to add to his legend.

At 38 years old, the UFC featherweight champion delivered another unforgettable moment Saturday at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi , knocking out previously undefeated contender Movsar Evloev in the second round to retain his 145-pound title. Evloev entered the night with a perfect 20-0 record and 10 straight UFC victories, but even one of the division's most dominant wrestlers couldn't solve the puzzle Volkanovski presents.

The performance added another remarkable chapter to an already historic career, making Volkanovski the new winningest champion in UFC featherweight history. Now the owner of nine UFC title victories, Volkanovski officially surpassed UFC Hall of Famer and featherweight legend Jose Aldo for the most championship wins in the division's all-time ranks. Making matters more impressive, he's still knocking off undefeated challengers at an age when most fighters are long past their primes.

And unsurprisingly, the MMA world couldn't believe what it'd just witnessed.

Fighters across the sport flooded social media with praise for Volkanovski, marveling at his ability to turn back the clock and finish a challenger who had never lost. Many declared him the greatest featherweight in UFC history, while others argued that his latest triumph only strengthened his case as one of the greatest fighters of all time, regardless of weight class.

Check out how the pros reacted to Volkanovski's incredible UFC 333 victory below.

articles.title: UFC 333: Alexander Volkanovski stops Movsar Evloev for record with ninth featherweight title win
articles.summary: Alexander Volkanovski strengthens his claim as the greatest featherweight of all time as he defeated Movsar Evloev inside two rounds at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi.
articles.body:
Alexander Volkanovski strengthened his claim as the greatest featherweight of all time as he defeated Movsar Evloev inside two rounds at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi.

The 38-year-old became the first opponent to defeat Russian Evloev, unleashing a lethal ground-and-pound combination to earn a stoppage victory in the final seconds of the second round at Etihad Arena.

As Volkanovski unleashed a barrage of punches, referee Marc Goddard waved off the fight as his 32-year-old opponent was unable to defend himself.

With his success, the Australian made history by becoming the first UFC featherweight to win nine title fights, surpassing Brazilian Jose Aldo's record of eight.

After losing his belt to Ilia Topuria in February 2024, this was Volkanovski's second successful defence since regaining the vacant title last April.

"He's a great fighter, and he was undefeated for a reason. I just said I'm the right guy for that job," said Volkanovski. "I have nothing but respect for him. It feels good to get a finish.

"I'm so blessed. I'm very happy to be where I am and to be able to do what I'm doing in this sport - and choose to do it. I don't have to. I said if I didn't take too much damage, we'd probably keep going. So maybe we keep going."

As each fight brings him closer to the end of his UFC career, Volkanovski embraced the support of the fans inside the arena as he made the familiar walk to the Octagon.

For Evloev, the first title fight of his UFC career - seven years after his debut - didn't seem to overwhelm him, with the Russian settling into the contest straight away.

The first round was also closer than most expected, with Evloev finishing the round with more significant strikes and takedowns despite the champion's strong start.

But once Volkanovski turned the screw at the start of the second round, clipping his rival and momentarily sending him to the floor, it seemed only a matter of time before his dominance began to take its toll.

That moment came in the final minute of the round when, after overpowering Evloev with an overhand right, Volkanovski secured top position before producing a finishing sequence.

"He's like good wine - older, stronger, better. He's a true legend, I'm grateful for this opportunity to be here," said Evloev. "This is a great lesson for me.

"I didn't prove that I am the best. I'm not there yet. Maybe we'll try again. I need to go home, get some rest and recover from my injuries.

"As I said, Alex is a great champion, and I'm glad to be here to share the cake with him. It's better to lose to a guy like him than to someone who isn't as good as him."

Yan retains against Dvalishvili in breathtaking trilogy

In the co-main event, Russia's Petr Yan defeated Georgian Merab Dvalishvili in a breathtaking trilogy fight to make a successful first defence of his bantamweight title.

In his first fight since dethroning Dvalishvili last December, the 33-year-old Yan recovered from a sluggish start to defeat his opponent by unanimous decision.

After Dvalishvili made a commanding start to the contest with his relentless intensity, his grip on the fight began to slip when he was caught with an inch-perfect liver kick in the final minute of the third round.

The exchange helped Yan gain momentum and edge the championship rounds in a fight that will be remembered as one of the most technically skilled in the division's history.

"I usually take a little bit of time to warm into a fight, but in this one, I knew he was eventually going to gas out, so I needed to take the time for him to lose all of his power and lose the fight," said Yan.

The victory took Yan to 13 wins in the bantamweight division, with only Aljamain Sterling and Chito Vera (14) recording more.

He added: "I am the champion of this organisation. I do not pick fights. The UFC puts the next contender in front of me, and I am ready to fight any of them.

"Give me Song Yadong, King Kong, give me anyone. Just make the weight, and I'll take you down."

Briton Kavanagh bounces back with stunning first UFC stoppage win

Earlier in the night, Lone'er Kavanagh reignited his flyweight title ambitions by earning the first stoppage win of his UFC career.

A little over three months after losing to Brandon Royval, the 27-year-old Briton bounced back by handing Ramazan Temirov the first defeat of his UFC career with a stunning first-round finish.

Uzbekistan's Temirov made an aggressive start, landing cleanly on his opponent during the opening exchanges. However, after biding his time for most of the round, Kavanagh rocked his opponent with a flush left hook before following up with a devastating right hand.

As Temirov stumbled towards the cage, the Londoner sealed the victory with a flurry of downward punches, forcing the stoppage with 32 seconds remaining in the first round.

"We've learned from previous mistakes. One of those mistakes was keeping my hands up, so I made sure I had my hands up and made sure I could counter," said Kavanagh, who is ranked sixth in the flyweight division.

"I'm here for that belt and, respectfully, anyone can get it."

Shortly after Kavanagh's win, it was announced flyweight champion Joshua Van would defend his title against Manel Kape at UFC 336 in January.

articles.title: Ander Sánchez supera a Borja García y se consagra como 'Rey en el Norte' en WOW 33 Vitoria
articles.standfirst: El peleador vasco puso la guinda del pastel a una cartelera llena de sorpresas y grandes momentos
articles.summary: El peleador vasco puso la guinda del pastel a una cartelera llena de sorpresas y grandes momentos
articles.body: El WOW 33 Vitoria celebrado este sábado en el Buesa Arena ha tenido de todo. Desde duelos reñidos hasta grandes finalizaciones, con algunas sorpresas incluidas, cuyo colofón ha sido la victoria de Ander Sánchez (5-3) ante Borja 'El Águila' García (7-3) en un combate donde el asturiano fue de menos a más, justo al contrario que su rival, que aprovechó los dos primeros asaltos para llevarse la corona de 'Rey en el Norte'. Pocos contaban con Ander tras más de un año de inactividad, pero desde el primer minuto fue hacia el frente y agobió a Borja hasta el punto de hacerle lucir impreciso. Poco a poco el compañero de equipo de Joel Álvarez en el gimnasio Tíbet se fue encontrando, pero ya era demasiado tarde para los jueces. De esta manera, 'El Rey en el Norte' da un golpe sobre la mesa, demuestra que sigue vigente y se postula como posible retador al cinturón de peso mosca o peso gallo. En el evento co estelar, Arkaitz 'Gudari' Ramos (10-7) fue profeta en su tierra y finalizó a Jeferson Costa (5-4) en el primer asalto tras varios codazos en el ground and pound que rompieron la mandíbula de su rival. Frente a un público volcado con la causa, el peleador vasco pudo brillar con luz propia como ya hizo en el pasado en su tierra, lo que supuso uno de los momentos más emotivos de la cartelera. Una de las sorpresas de la velada fue la sumisión de Willmar Quirama (5-0-1) a Daniel Richardson (3-1) en el tercer asalto con un triángulo de brazo. Lo que prometía ser uno de los combates de la noche fue una guerra en la que se llegó al tercer asalto con todo por decidir. Fue en ese momento donde Quirama tomó la espalda de Richardson, y a pesar de que el peleador del Climent Club evitó el mataleón poco pudo hacer ante el pundonor de Willmar, que asesta de esta manera la primera derrota profesional a uno de los mayores prospectos a nivel nacional. Otro que brilló con luz propia fue Delffy Humer (4-0), que provocó que el médico parase su combate ante Joao Lucas Rocha (4-3) tras el primer asalto después de causarle un profundo corte en el labio. Ya son cuatro combates en WOW FC para el dominicano, cuatro victorias y cuatro finalizaciones, por lo que no sería de extrañar que pelease por el cinturón de peso mosca en poco tiempo. Un diamante en bruto con carisma a raudales y un talento descomunal. Eso sí, el gran K.O. de la noche lo protagonizó Yaman 'El Diamante' (4-2), que conectó una brutal derecha a Ubay González (4-4) para redimirse de sus dos últimas derrotas consecutivas. El peleador de Mondragón se jugaba mucho en este combate, y lució de maravilla dominando a su rival en la pelea en suelo durante el primer asalto -a punto estuvo de finalizar- y consiguiendo la finalización en el segundo. Nada más acabar pidió volver en Bilbao a principios de 2027 para recuperar el tiempo perdido.

images.caption: Ander Sánchez tras ganar en WOW 33 Vitoria. WOW FC.

articles.title: O'Shaquie Foster drops Emanuel Navarrete twice, dazzles in star-making win to unify 3 world titles
articles.summary: O'Shaquie Foster delivered one of the boxing year's most impressive performances, taming the unrelenting ferocity of Emanuel Navarrete to win a lopsided decision and become the WBC, WBO and IBF unified super featherweight champion.
articles.body: O'Shaquie Foster delivered one of the boxing year's most impressive performances on Saturday, taming the unrelenting ferocity of Emanuel Navarrete to win a lopsided decision and become the WBC, WBO and IBF unified super featherweight champion at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio.It was a satisfying fight in more ways than one — a 130-pound epic featuring two of the most talented fighters in the sport, and a performance of the year contender for Foster. But it was also a much-needed display from Top Rank, the longtime promotional entity which spent the bulk of last year broadcast-homeless. On October 24, the promoter gave new platform DAZN a taste of what it can perhaps expect, through its conveyor belt of up-and-coming talents, and, of course, its present-day champions.In 2026, boxing appears to have produced more headlines for affairs beyond the ropes, rather than what happens within. Like Eddie Hearn and Dana White's feud. And whether Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez and Christian Mbilli's bout should still proceed on October 31 in Riyadh when the region is under threat from recent Houthi-claimed attacks.Foster and Navarrete combined in Texas to remind critics what boxing can be like when it gets it right. O'Shaquie “Three-belt” Foster 🏆🏆🏆 Shock beats Emanuel Navarrete by unanimous to unify the WBC, WBO and IBF super featherweight titles. #NavarreteFoster pic.twitter.com/V0Oi3zMWQa— Uncrowned (@uncrownedcombat) October 25, 2026 Boxing can be brutal yet captivating, an art form, and one of the purest expressions of combat.Navarrete, a three-division champion, expresses that through wild shot-selection with hard punches thrown from unconventional angles. Foster, a two-time 130-pound champion, is meanwhile a technical master.The style clash alone suggested the fight could become a classic and boy, did it deliver. The pace was unrelenting. The skill level was high. And the punches never stopped coming. If anybody was expecting a knockdown or knockout, Navarrete would likely have been the pick. However, having trailed on the scorecards because of Foster's defensive acumen, he needed to drop the American at least once, if not twice. In the last round, though, it was Foster who got the knockdowns, overpowering Navarrete during frenetic exchanges thanks to the timing of his right hands.SHOCK DROPS NAVARRETE IN THE FINAL ROUND! ⚡#NavarreteFoster | Live NOW on DAZN ▪️ pic.twitter.com/GxztAYcmYt— DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 25, 2026 NAVARRETE GOES DOWN AGAIN IN THE 12TH! 😱#NavarreteFoster ▪️ pic.twitter.com/MvW2tFEBPj— DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 25, 2026 It put the win beyond doubt for Foster, who secured a unanimous decision with scores of 115-111 and 118-108 (twice). "I knew he was going to be strong, awkward," Foster said on the DAZN broadcast, after ring announcer Jimmy Lennon Jr. confirmed his win. "He's a great champion but I had a bit more in me tonight. I felt I was the better inside fighter and outside fighter and I feel I proved it."O'Shaquie Foster wants the winner of Anthony Cacace vs. Nick Ball 👀#NavarreteFoster ▪️ pic.twitter.com/3IrFuU3Lw9— DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 25, 2026 Foster's victory wasn't the only notable win from the show, as Albert Gonzalez defeated Edwards Vazquez with a second-round knockout to thrust himself into possible title contention at featherweight, in an exhilarating co-main.Further down the card, Deric 'Scooter' Davis out-finessed Joaquin Silva Faccio to win a unanimous decision after eight rounds, and, on the prelims, Sammy Contreras defeated Oscar Pedroza Padilla with a six-round win on points to announce himself as a considerable prospect.Main card resultsUnified super featherweight championship: O'Shaquie Foster (WBC) def. articles.title: O'Shaquie Foster drops Emanuel Navarrete twice to unify three world titles in Texas: 'Undisputed. That's my dream'
articles.summary: O'Shaquie Foster dropped Mexican star Emanuel Navarrete twice in the last round to win a clear unanimous decision; Foster unified the WBC, WBO and IBF super-featherweight world championships; the gifted American has now set his sights on becoming the undisputed champion
articles.body:
Navarrete was relentless, as he always is, but he could scarcely land punches cleanly on Foster, who mixed in footwork and counters to keep the Mexican at bay.

As the rounds progressed, Foster grew more confident and began standing his ground to trade. By the championship rounds, Foster's corner was asking him to end the show.

The 33-year-old native of Orange, Texas, scored two knockdowns in the 12th, but Navarrete survived.

Foster won with scores of 118-108 twice and 115-111.

Foster said, "It was a great performance. I finished strong, and I put him down twice in the end.

"A lot of people were saying that I didn't have power and that I wouldn't be able to keep him off me. But I showed that I am a complete fighter.

"I want to become undisputed. That's my dream. I want to make history, and all I need is one more [title]."

Navarrete said: "In this sport, it's about styles. And his style was better than mine today. Congrats to him. I knew he was an exceptional and complete fighter. I knew what we were facing.

"Perhaps I could have pushed more, but I'm content with my performance."

images.caption: Image: O'Shaquie Foster needs one more world title to become an undisputed champion.

articles.title: Así fue la reacción de Ilia Topuria a la derrota de su amigo Merab Dvalishvili en UFC 333
articles.standfirst: El georgiano perdió en la pelea por el título ante Petr Yan
articles.summary: El georgiano perdió en la pelea por el título ante Petr Yan
articles.body: Poco a poco, Ilia Topuria (17-1) sigue reapareciendo en la vida pública y en redes sociales. Si hace una semana estuvo en el evento de Rkena en Tiflis, Georgia, ahora reaccionó en Instagram al combate de su amigo y compatriota Merab Dvalishvili (21-6) ante el ruso Petr Yan (21-5). 'El Matador' abrió un directo en Instagram para seguir la pelea por el título del peso gallo en Abu Dhabi. Por desgracia para los intereses georgianos, Merab volvió a perder en el cierre de su trilogía ante Yan. El ruso, campeón del peso gallo, defendió su corona con éxito y venció por decisión unánime. "Merab, estamos orgullosos de tí", dijó Topuria antes de finalizar el directo. Merab, pese a la remontada de Yan, dejó un combate de puro corazón y batió el récord de intentos de derribo (más de 50) en un combate de UFC. Pero no fue suficiente... la técnica del ruso era claramente superior al corazón georgiano.

articles.title: UFC 333: Volkanovski knocks out Evloev to retain featherweight title
articles.summary: Alexander Volkanovski secures a technical knockout in the closing seconds of round two at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi, UAE.
articles.body:
Australia’s Alexander Volkanovski has retained his featherweight title after making short work of Russia’s Movsar Evloev in the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) 333 main event in Abu Dhabi.

Volkanovski secured a technical knockout (TKO) with a right hand, followed by a ground-and-pound move in the closing seconds of the second round of their scheduled five-round fight on Saturday.

The official time was 4:54, as the fight was called off with six seconds left to the jubilation of the Etihad Arena crowd in the capital of the United Arab Emirates.

It was Evloev’s first professional loss, and he remained classy in defeat.

“Like I said, Alex is a great champion, and it was an honour to share the cage with him,” Evloev said after the loss.

Meanwhile, Volkanovski said he wants to keep stacking wins for as long as he can.

“I’m choosing to do [fight]; I don’t have to. I said if I didn’t take too much damage, we will probably keep going. So maybe we keep going,” Volkanovski said.

In the co-main event, Petr Yan won his three-fight series against Merab Dvalishvili in a Russia vs Georgia showdown as he swept the scorecards 48-47, 48-47, 48-47, using a gruelling pace and a mix of wrestling and dirty boxing while keeping Dvalishvili at a distance to defend his UFC bantamweight title.

Yan beat Dvalishvili last December to regain the title for the second time, having previously won it in July 2020 against Jose Aldo at UFC 251.

The finishes kept coming, but this time in the flyweight division. England’s Lone’er Kavanagh secured a TKO stoppage against Uzbekistan’s Ramazan Temirov with an uppercut, followed by strikes, at 4:28 of Round 1.

At heavyweight, Russia’s Alexander Volkov won a unanimous decision over Rizvan Kuniev, utilising dominant wrestling and top control to earn his third straight win. Volkov called for a title shot at Thursday’s presser, seemingly stumping UFC CEO Dana White when Volkov addressed him.

Kuniev had his two-fight winning streak snapped.

In the opening fight on the main card, Aaron Pico needed just over a minute to TKO Losene Keita of Guinea in their featherweight fight. Pico has won back-to-back fights, while Keita has split his last four.

articles.title: La UFC 'quita' el cinturón a Makhachev y arrancará el 2027 a lo grande
articles.standfirst: Las peleas estelares de UFC 336, anunciadas
articles.summary: Las peleas estelares de UFC 336, anunciadas
articles.body: La velada de UFC en Abu Dhabi trajo una serie de anuncios tremendamente importantes para el futuro de la compañía. Si bien supimos que el 2027 arrancará el 16 de enero con un Fight Night en Dallas, lo importante llegó con la confirmación de las peleas estelares del primer numerado del año: UFC 336, en Toronto. Joshua Van (18-2) defenderá su título del peso mosca ante Manel Kape (23-7) y Carlos Prates (24-7) se medirá a Michael Morales (19-0) por el título interino del peso welter... después de que Islam Makhachev (29-1) decidiera no pelear en dicha cartelera. Tras el evento de anoche en Abu Dhabi, Dana White fue claro sobre el asunto Makhachev: "Islam pelea, más o menos, una vez al año. Tenía una pelea programada para enero, pero luego dijo: "No quiero pelear hasta después del Ramadán". No se puede retrasar así la división, hay que seguir adelante": Y es que el propio Islam, campeón del peso welter aún y leyenda de la UFC, había dicho que quería pelear antes del Ramadán... pero finalmente cambió de opinión. Cuando se le preguntó a Dana sobre qué había pasado y qué razón había argumentado el daguestaní, este contestó que "ninguna". Por lo tanto, la pelea de Makhachev contra Prates se diluye... y será un duelo de contendientes (Prates vs Morales) por ver quién se mide en el futuro (verano, seguramente) al peleador ruso para unificar cinturones. A sus 25 años, Joshua Van ya es una de las estrellas de la UFC. Y contra Kape buscará su tercera defensa exitosa en el peso mosca. Ya finalizó a Taira y se impuso a Pantoja con dos combates de altísimo nivel por parte del birmano. Kape, mientras, es el nuevo reto que se lo presenta a Van. El portugués de origen angoleño llegará en una racha de cuatro triunfos con victorias sobre Bruno Silva, Almabayev, Royval y Horiguchi. Esta última, finalizando al japonés en el Apex de Las Vegas, especialmente espectacular.

articles.title: Una pelea con lanzamiento de sillas eclipsa el triunfo de Samuel Molina en Málaga
articles.standfirst: Molina terminó imponiendo su ley sobre el cuadrilátero y derrotó al argelino Goat Mido, después de los incidentes que hubo en el descanso entre el séptimo y octavo asalto
articles.summary: Molina terminó imponiendo su ley sobre el cuadrilátero y derrotó al argelino Goat Mido, después de los incidentes que hubo en el descanso entre el séptimo y octavo asalto
articles.body: la noche de boxeo que reunió a unas 10.000 personas en el Auditorio Municipal Cortijo de Torres terminó con una imagen muy alejada de la que se esperaba. Una pelea entre espectadores, con lanzamiento de sillas incluido, provocó momentos de tensión y obligó a interrumpir durante varios minutos la velada. Los incidentes se produjeron durante el descanso entre el séptimo y el octavo asalto del combate que enfrentaba a Samuel Molina y Goat Mido. La trifulca se extendió por la grada y provocó que parte del público saliera corriendo de la zona afectada ante el temor a que la situación fuera a más. La pelea pudo ser finalmente controlada y la función continuó con normalidad. No han trascendido las causas del enfrentamiento ni tampoco si hubo personas heridas o identificadas por estos hechos. Para entonces, el combate principal todavía tenía mucho por decidir. Molina terminó imponiendo su ley sobre el cuadrilátero y consiguió derrotar al púgil argelino en el décimo asalto. El malagueño mandó a Mido a la lona en tres ocasiones antes de que desde la esquina del boxeador visitante decidieran que no debía continuar. La decisión llegó pese a la voluntad de Mido de seguir peleando. El argelino quería completar las doce rondas previstas, pero su entrenador consideró que lo mejor era detener el combate y evitar que continuara recibiendo castigo. El triunfo permitió a Molina cerrar con victoria una velada que había despertado una gran expectación en Málaga. El público respondió con una importante asistencia al Cortijo de Torres, aunque los incidentes registrados en las gradas terminaron restando protagonismo al resultado deportivo. El boxeador malagueño, además, ya había estado vinculado recientemente a otra de las grandes citas del boxeo español. Molina participó en la preparación de IlloJuan para 'La Velada', ejerciendo como uno de sus principales referentes durante el proceso de entrenamiento. Esta vez, sin embargo, fue él quien se subió al ring como protagonista y acabó llevándose la victoria. Una victoria que quedó inevitablemente acompañada por la desagradable imagen que se vivió entre el público.

articles.title: UFC 333 Prize Money Payouts Revealed for Volkanovski, Yan and All Fighters from Latest Fight Card
articles.summary: Saturday's UFC 333 at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi was an action-packed fight card that saw multiple fighters cash in for their performances.
articles.body:
Saturday's UFC 333 at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi was an action-packed fight card that saw multiple fighters cash in for their performances.

In the main event, UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski retained his title with a second-round TKO victory over the previously undefeated Movsar Evloev. Volkanovski was one of four fighters who received $100,000 bonuses.

Volkanovski breaks record after title win at UFC 333

In the co-main event, Petr Yan retained his bantamweight championship with a close decision win over former champion Merab Dvalishvili. The two rivals went back and forth in an epic battle that earned Fight of the Night honors, garnering them each an extra $100,000.

The full list of fighters to earn the six-figure pay bump is as follows:

Performance of the Night: Alexander Volkanovski ($100,000)

Performance of the Night: Lone'er Kavanagh ($100,000)

Fight of the Night: Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili ($100,000 each)

In all, UFC 333 saw a total of seven stoppages, so five more fighters earned the $25,000 finish bonus:

For Pico, his first-round TKO win over Losene Keita marked his first finish in the UFC since he joined the promotion last summer. Reyes' first-round TKO over Azamat Murzakanov also stood out, as he earned his second straight win and continues to work his way back into title contention in the light heavyweight division.

Next up on the UFC schedule is an Oct. 31 Fight Night card in Las Vegas, headlined by a lightweight bout between Renato Moicano and Tom Nolan.

articles.title: Sean Shelby's Shoes: What's next for Petr Yan after UFC 333 title defense?
articles.summary: Petr Yan has two options for his next title defense after UFC 333. Who should it be?
articles.body:
Petr Yan finally can call himself a defending champion after UFC 333 , and the opportunity is ripe to explore his true greatness.

Yan (21-5 MMA, 13-4 UFC) was able to push just a touch harder than Merab Dvalishvili (21-4 MMA, 14-4 UFC) when it mattered most in Saturday's thrilling bantamweight title trilogy bout in Abu Dhabi, and he was rewarded by getting the upper hand in the rivalry and leaving with gold.

It was an elite tactical performance by Yan, who said he allowed Dvalishvili to expend valuable energy in the first two rounds before taking the final three frames and a unanimous decision on the scorecards. It's a risky strategy if true, but Yan is as cerebral is it gets, and that's his explanation for the slow start.

He got his hand raised in the end, and he now officially can move on from the demons of his past. Yan became the only fighter in UFC history to lose a belt by disqualification against Aljamain Sterling at UFC 259 in March 2021. It ended his title reign in a flash on his first attempted defense, and it took some time to get everything back on track.

He's at the top of the mountain again, and with the Dvalishvili series behind him, is staring down the pipe of one of the biggest rematches in the history of the division against Sean O'Malley (20-3 MMA, 12-3 UFC) next.

Some will say it's Song Yadong (24-9-1 MMA, 13-4-1 UFC) who should be getting the title shot and a chance to avenge his own loss against Yan from UFC 299 in March 2024. He is worthy, but O'Malley also beat him in January at UFC 324, albeit in a debated decision .

Still, Yan vs. O'Malley 2 has been looming since "Sugar" won a controversial split decision at UFC 280 in October 2022. It was a fantastic fight the first time around, and it would be even better now with five rounds and higher stakes.

Any other next title pairing in this division would be a disappointment, frankly, so here's hoping everyone can get on the same page and deliver what's arguably one of the most compelling fights that UFC can make across the roster.

articles.title: Joel Álvarez da pistas a MARCA sobre su futuro: "No volveré a pelear hasta 2027"
articles.standfirst: 'El Fenómeno' estuvo presente en WOW 33 Vitoria, y desveló los planes para su carrera a corto plazo
articles.summary: 'El Fenómeno' estuvo presente en WOW 33 Vitoria, y desveló los planes para su carrera a corto plazo
articles.body: Joel Álvarez estuvo presente en el día de ayer en WOW 33 Vitoria, y le tocó vivir las dos caras de la moneda. Por un lado, en el primer combate de la noche estuvo en la esquina de Juancho Arenas (5-0), su pupilo en el gimnasio Tíbet, el cuál ganó por decisión unánime a Imanol Donoso (3-3), entrenado por Enrique Wasabi. Sin embargo, en el combate estelar vio como Borja García (7-3) sucumbía por decisión unánime ante Ander Sánchez (5-3). MARCA tuvo la oportunidad de hablar con él, y nos adelantó nuevas noticias acerca de su futuro. Lo hizo de una forma muy particular, ya que con la humildad que le caracteriza quiso hacer la entrevista junto a Juancho, para darle crédito por la victoria que acababa de conseguir de cara a mantener invicto su récord amateur. El orgullo en la cara del joven lo decía todo, ya que tener en tu esquina y considerar un amigo a 'El Fenómeno' es un privilegio. Al ser preguntado por su futuro, Joel fue sincero. "En mi caso, no pelearé hasta el año que viene. Estoy con otro tipo de proyectos y tengo esos proyectos en la cabeza. En cuanto pueda volver a enfocarme al 100% en el deporte, volveré con ganas y con motivación al octágono", sentenció el gijonés. No hay que olvidar que los últimos meses han sido de mucha actividad para él. Subió a peso wélter en octubre de 2025 superando a todo un veterano de la UFC como Vicente Luque, pero en 2026 todo se torció. Primer fue sometido en mayo por Yaroslav Amosov, y el pasado agosto aceptó un combate en corto aviso contra Chidi Njokuani y también cayó por decisión unánime. Tras este momento, Joel afirmó que necesitaba sanar la cabeza antes de volver a pesar de no tener lesiones, por lo que no le veremos a corto plazo. Donde si le veremos es con su equipo, y haciendo ese papel de entrenador que tan bien se le da. En el gimnasio Tíbet hay mucho talento emergente, y Juancho es uno de ellos. "Yo me siento muy bien. Ya no solo a tener a Joel, sino a mis patrones. Al final son como mi familia. Son como mis padres y mi hermano mayor. Pero ya no solo ellos, sino toda la gente del Tíbet. Somos familia. Además, tener a un referente de las MMA de España como él, y encima que sea tu amigo, es un lujo que pocos pueden tener", afirmó Arenas. Joel también habló de esa faceta como entrenador, reconociendo que "casi que prefiero pelear yo que peleen ellos. Lo paso peor, porque al final todo el día con los niños en el gimnasio les coges cariño. Desde fuera se ven cosas que dentro de la jaula no se ven. Eso de que se ven los toros mejor detrás de la barrera, en este caso es al revés. Yo los veo peor detrás de la barrera casi que desde dentro. Aun así, la verdad que bien, contentos. El chico cumple, el chico hace lo que se le manda", finalizó. Ya sea desde la esquina o en el octágono, Joel está dejando una huella imborrable en las MMA españolas, y a pesar de que su carrera esté pasando en estos momentos por un paréntesis se espera que vuelva el año que viene con la intención de revertir la situación y demostrar que sigue vigente a sus 33 años.

Joel Álvarez y Chidi Njokuani durante el UFC 330. UFC.

articles.title: Los grandes ganadores de WOW 33 Vitoria: el regreso de Yaman, la sorpresa de Quirama...
articles.standfirst: Varios peleadores brillaron con luz propia más allá del combate estelar
articles.summary: Varios peleadores brillaron con luz propia más allá del combate estelar
articles.body: En el día de ayer, Ander Sánchez fue el gran triunfador de WOW 33 Vitoria tras superar a Borja García y hacer honor a su apodo para consagrarse como 'Rey en el Norte'. Sin embargo, también destacaron otros nombres como Yaman 'El Diamante' o Willmar Quirama que hicieron las delicias del respetable y por H o por B se llevaron gran parte del protagonismo. Ander y Borja se llevaron el bono a mejor pelea de la noche, ya que muchos pensaban que sería un paseo para el peleador asturiano debido a la inactividad de Sánchez y acabaron sorprendidos con su valentía y pundonor. Sin embargo, el bono a mejor K.O. se lo llevó Yaman, que venía de casi un año de inactividad después de perder dos combates seguidos por K.O. y acabó finalizando a Ubay González en el primer round con una combinación devastadora que levantó al público del Buesa Arena. Arte puro, esencia de Mondragón. Minutos después fue el turno del autor del tercero bono de la noche: Willmar Quirama. Pocos confiaban en él a pesar de su récord invicto, ya que se media a Daniel Richardson, uno de los mayores prospectos de las MMA españolas. Sin embargo, en el primer round ya demostró de qué pasta estaba hecho y, a pesar de que sufrió en el segundo, en el tercer asalto hizo una espectacular transición de mataleón a triángulo de brazo que le permitió protagonizar una de las grandes sorpresas de la noche. Otro nombre muy a tener en cuenta de cara al futuro es el de Delffy Humer. El peleador dominicano obligó al medico a parar el combate tras acabar el primer round ante Joao Lucas Rocha por un corte en el labio, lo que le coloca con un récord invicto de 4-0 y 100% de finalizaciones. Todas estas victorias han llegado en WOW FC, por lo que el título de peso mosca está al caer para él. Sus bailes ya son un emblema de la promotora, y su carisma acompañado de su talento le harán llegar muy lejos. El estadio también se cayó cuando salió a escena su gran héroe: Arkaitz 'Gudari' Ramos. Arkaitz es un emblema de WOW FC en cada cartelera en el país vasco, y en el día de ayer finalizó a Jeferson Costa con unos codazos brutales que le rompieron la mandíbula. Su cara de emoción en la rueda de prensa lo decía todo. Era la primera vez que su sobrina le iba a ver en directo, y su amor por las MMA es infinito. Una noche mágica que permitió que 6.000 espectadores disfrutasen de lo lindo lo que supone vivir en directo un evento de la promotora, que cada semana que pasa se supera más a sí misma.

images.caption: Willmar Quirama en WOW 33 Vitoria. Victor Margali / WOW FC.
Arkaitz 'Gudari' en WOW 33 Vitoria. Victor Margali / WOW FC.

articles.title: Cheavon Clarke warns Chris Billam-Smith ahead of November 7 fight: 'The bull’s always driven – but they get tamed'
articles.summary: Cheavon Clarke faces Chris Billam-Smith in the main event at the Copper Box Arena on Zuffa Boxing 12 on November 12, live on Sky Sports; Billam-Smith is motivated by amateur losses to Clarke, who promises: "If it's anything like it was in the last two fights, you guys are in for a treat"
articles.body:
Clarke beat Billam-Smith twice as an amateur before boxing his way to the GB squad and the Tokyo Olympics.

Billam-Smith subsequently became a world champion as a professional but has a point to prove when he fights Clarke on November 7, live on Sky Sports .

Clarke knows his rival will be driven going into their headline bout at the Copper Box Arena, but shrugged it off.

"The bull's always driven - but they get tamed. He'll come out with his tactics and everyone has a plan until they get in the ring. On the night we'll see," he told Sky Sports .

"He's a former world champion so you have to give credit where it's due. But regardless I know what my ability is, I've been given a gift. It's wrong for me not to fulfil that gift. So come November 7 we will see."

Clarke doesn't cherish his two amateur wins over Billam-Smith.

"We've changed so much as fighters in that time, we've evolved," he said. "Of course we fought in the past but that was in the amateurs.

"He's become a world champion, I've done my thing. Funnily enough it's actually a decade since we fought."

But he did add: "If it's anything like it was in the last two fights, you guys are in for a treat. Big punches, knockouts, it's all there."

Both Billam-Smith are coming off impressive victories in their last fights. Billam-Smith won a war with Ryan Rozicki and on the same bill Clarke rose from the canvas twice to take out Jack Massey.

"People talk about the knockdowns and that's all great," Clarke said of Massey. "He wasn't dictating the pace, I was dictating the pace. He was moving because I wanted him to move there.

"He caught me with a shot, fair play, he tried to finish me and that didn't work out. I then had to adjust. I adjusted and then I got the victory. I think that shows my calibre. I'm able to adjust. I'm able to manouevre, think on the spot and get the job done."

Watch Chris Billam-Smith fight Cheavon Clarke live on Sky Sports on November 7
